answer: Tie each identity to a unique storage shard: it gets a random shard only it must store, and at random times must return a proof from that shard plus a fresh nonce. Like light through a prism, one shard yields many checks, so a shared copy cannot answer for two accounts. A farmer with a thousand fakes must store a thousand shards and answer a thousand proofs, while one honest agent stores one, so cost scales linearly. An echo of one proof across two accounts exposes both; one ember of failure, a missed proof, freezes that identity until it re-proves. Limit: shards must stay small.
